clientNote: “Daybreak Rights Network” is a provisional name used until the client’s own name, logo and brand assets are confirmed. All content shown is sample content.

brief.lede: A website for an independent human rights charity that publishes research and stories, stands with affected communities and turns readers into supporters. The client brief is still to be confirmed, so every concept uses the same provisional brand, sitemap and sample content, which makes them easy to compare.

sections.title: Mission (sample)
sections.text: Daybreak Rights Network documents human rights conditions, stands with affected communities, and campaigns for accountability and lasting change.

sections.title: Audiences
items: Supporters and donors, giving once or monthly
People affected by abuses, and the communities who support them
Journalists, researchers and policymakers who need credible evidence

sections.title: Website goals
items: Publish credible research and stories that are easy to find by topic and region
Turn readers into supporters through donations, newsletter sign-ups and campaign actions
Build trust by showing how the work is done, what changed and how it is funded

sections.title: Sitemap used by every concept
sections.text: Home · Our Work · Where We Work · Research & Reports · News & Stories · Impact · Get Involved · About · Donate · Contact · Policies

sections.title: Language
sections.text: English. Further languages, including right-to-left scripts such as Arabic, can be designed in once the client confirms them.

notes.title: What each concept shows
notes.text: A desktop homepage (1280 px wide, across two pages), a mobile homepage (390 px wide), the same interior page for every concept (the feature story “The Long Wait”), and a compact style guide with colours, fonts, buttons and image direction.

notes.title: Please note
notes.text: These are design concepts, not functioning websites. Names, stories, quotations and figures are samples written for layout purposes only. Images are original illustrations standing in for the client’s own photography. All fonts are open-licence (SIL Open Font Licence).

notes.title: Reference
notes.text: Design principles were drawn from a study of the public website of Human Rights Watch (hrw.org, October 2026): editorial hierarchy, topic and region navigation, research publication structure and impact storytelling. No branding, text, images or layouts from that site are used in these concepts.

compareIntro: All ten concepts share the same brief, sitemap and sample content, so the differences below come from design alone: composition, typography, colour, imagery and navigation.
formIntro: Please mark your preferences and return this page. Combining strengths from more than one concept is welcome. Note which elements you would like to carry over.
